speaker: Sheldon
text: Same paradox. If you were to travel back in time and say, knock me unconscious, you would not then have the conversation that irritated you, motivating you to go back and knock me unconscious. It won't change the past.

speaker: Leonard
text: Can I go back and prevent you from explaining that to me? What if I knock you unconscious right now?

speaker: Leonard
text: But it'd make the present so much nicer.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, it was a number of things. First, the late hour, then your demeanor seems very low energy, plus your irritability.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh. I don't usually pick up on those things. Good for me.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, wait. Did you want to talk about what's bothering you?

speaker: Leonard
text: Here's the thing. The girls like Penny never end up with guys who own time machines.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I disagree. But your inability to successfully woo Penny long predates your acquisition of the time machine.

speaker: Sheldon
text: That failure clearly stands on its own.

speaker: Sheldon
text: In addition, your premise is flawed. In the original film, Rod Taylor got Yvette Mimieux with that very time machine. In Back to the Future, Marty McFly got the opportunity to hook up with his extremely attractive young mother.
